# A Quiet Moment

The morning light falls soft and slow,
On grass still wet with gentle dew,
A bird calls out a song we know,
While sky wears its pale, patient blue.

The world is still, the air is sweet,
No rush, no noise to break the spell,
Just earth and sky in balance meet,
And all the quiet stories they tell.

So pause a moment, breathe it in,
This peace that asks for nothing more—
Just notice where the day begins,
And all the beauty at your door.

# Autumn's End

The leaves fall down like letters never sent,
Each one a word I couldn't find to say.
The autumn comes to show me what was spent—
The warmth we had has turned to cold and gray.

I walk these streets where echoes live alone,
Past empty benches where we used to sit.
The world moves on; I cannot find the tone
To sing again, though I have not yet quit.

The rain falls soft on all the things we lost,
The promises we made but couldn't keep.
Some seasons come too soon, and count the cost—
And all I have are hours left to weep.

Yet still, somewhere, a single bird will sing,
And maybe that's enough to carry through—
That even in the dying of the spring,
Some small, soft light remembers loving you.

# A Little Joy

The sun breaks through the morning gray,
And paints the world in gold,
A gentle breeze whispers "hello,"
To stories yet untold.

A smile spreads without a reason,
A laugh that bubbles free,
The simple gift of being alive—
Of all that you can be.

Birds sing their carefree melodies,
Flowers dance and sway,
And in this moment, bright and warm,
All worries fade away.

So take this day and hold it close,
Let happiness take flight,
For joy lives in the smallest things—
A spark, a flame, a light. ✨
